en.name: Paul
en.summary: A former persecutor of Christians converted on the road to Damascus, whose missionary journeys and letters shaped the early Church.
en.body: Paul, originally called Saul, was a Pharisee who actively persecuted the early Christian community until, according to Acts, a vision of the risen Christ on the road to Damascus converted him. He was not one of the original Twelve but is traditionally counted among the apostles for his direct commission and his enormous influence: his missionary journeys across the eastern Mediterranean established churches from Antioch to Rome, and his letters make up a large part of the New Testament. Tradition holds he was martyred by beheading in Rome, and he is honoured jointly with Peter as co-patron of the city.
